disease_label_per_paper: Confirmed toxic shock syndrome associated with menstrual cup use
presentation_summary: 37-year-old woman presented with a two-day history of fevers, conjunctival hyperemia, abdominal cramps, myalgias, vaginal discharge, and diffuse erythroderma after recent menstrual cup use.
Initial exam: looked unwell, oral temperature 37.2 C, blood pressure 98/65 mmHg, heart rate 132/min; no other obvious source of sepsis.
Within 24 hours she deteriorated with temperature 39.1 C, blood pressure 76/45 mmHg, heart rate 137/min, persistent hypotension despite fluids and antibiotics.

Laboratory results included WBC 23.6 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 72 g/L, platelets 107 x10^9/L, INR 1.8, fibrinogen 4.79 g/L, creatinine 106 umol/L, CK 346 U/L, ALT 52 U/L, AST 72 U/L, bilirubin 61.3 umol/L, potassium 3.0 mmol/L.
Postadmission day 2: generalized morbilliform rash; desquamation began on postadmission day 4 after clindamycin was added.

risk_context.source_text_value: began using The DivaCup 10 days before presentation; reported small abrasion during insertion

confirmatory_findings.finding: Clinical case definition met for non-streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: article diagnosis: confirmed case of toxic shock syndrome associated with menstrual cup use

confirmatory_findings.finding: Cultures did not identify another bloodstream/urinary/respiratory source
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: blood and urine cultures, MRSA screening, C. difficile toxin assay and respiratory viral swab were negative

actual_treatment: intravenous clindamycin added after Infectious Diseases consultation
quality_warnings: Culture-negative menstrual TSS is stored as a clinical confirmed case; culture results are in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary diagnostic evidence.
The runtime observations use the early deterioration window because this is when the defining hypotension and fever were documented.
